Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.

Recycled language: friendly, nice, kind.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (9 items):

friendly — kind and pleasant to others. Example: The staff are friendly.
nice — pleasant, good. Example: She is a nice person.
kind — caring about other people. Example: He is kind to animals.
funny — making people laugh. Example: My cousin is very funny.
polite — showing good manners. Example: Be polite to the guests.
angry — feeling strong displeasure. Example: He is angry about the delay.
quiet — with little noise, or not talking much. Example: She is quiet in meetings.
lazy — not wanting to work. Example: He is a bit lazy in the morning.
serious — not joking, thoughtful. Example: My colleague is serious.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What is she like?
• She is very kind.
• He is quiet but funny.
• I think he is polite.
• He is a bit lazy.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'kind and pleasant to others'?
Which word means 'pleasant, good'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
Stress both adjectives when they are linked.
She is KIND and FUNny.
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Be + adjective.
Use be + adjective for personality: She is friendly. Link two adjectives with and or but: He is quiet but funny.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct connector.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My neighbour is friendly and kind. She is quiet but very funny. Her son is polite but a little lazy. My colleague is serious and hard-working.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What is your new colleague like? B: He is polite and serious. A: Is he funny? B: No, he is quiet.
Speaking: pair work

• What is she like?
• She is very kind.
• He is quiet but funny.
Writing: short text
